title: Asset Liability Management defends the peg in both directions with two separate reserves
content:
A.3.3.1.1 and A.3.3.1.2 define a matched pair. Actively Stabilizing Collateral is "highly liquid market making non-USDS assets that trade for close to 1 USD per USDS," so that "if there is ever downward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to buy USDS to maintain the peg." The Demand Absorption Buffer is "highly liquid market making USDS assets," so that "if there is ever upward pressure on the price of USDS these assets can be used to sell USDS to maintain the peg."

Treating the upside as a problem is the non-obvious half. A stablecoin trading above peg is usually read as a success, but persistent premium means the coin is not fungible with a dollar, arbitrage is being left on the table, and holders who need to exit at par cannot. The DAB is inventory held specifically to sell into that demand — Sky commits to being a market maker on both sides rather than only a defender of the floor.

The sizing is asymmetric: 5% of the Collateral Portfolio in ASC (A.3.3.2.2), and a DAB "equal to 25% of their required Actively Stabilizing Collateral" (A.3.3.2.3), i.e. 1.25% of the portfolio. Four times as much firepower is held for defending the floor as for capping the ceiling — reasonable, since a discount is a solvency signal that feeds on itself while a premium is self-correcting through USDS issuance.

A.3.3 frames the whole framework as replacing "Sky Core's historical Asset Liability Management mechanisms," which are to be "offboarded entirely or transitioned to Prime Agents." Peg defense is being moved from a central treasury function to a distributed obligation on the Agents who hold the collateral.
description: ASC is non-USDS assets ready to buy USDS under downward pressure; the Demand Absorption Buffer is USDS ready to sell under upward pressure, sized at 25% of the ASC requirement.
